metadata.note: The Lehigh and Hudson River Railway, Greycourt NY - Warwick - Belvidere NJ (with trackage rights over the PRR Belvidere Delaware to Phillipsburg and its own bridge into Easton PA), and its Orange County Railroad leg Greycourt - Maybrook; plus the line's predecessor the Warwick Valley Railroad, Greycourt - Warwick, worked by the Erie 1862-1880 and by itself 1880-1882. Consolidated 1 Apr 1882; full line opened 14 Aug 1882; last passenger train 8 Jul 1939 (Greycourt - Warwick); freight only thereafter, to Conrail 1976. Research report: research/branches/lehigh_and_hudson_river_railway.txt.

segments.note: The Warwick Valley Railroad (chartered 1860) opened Greycourt - Warwick on 1 Apr 1862 ("On April 1, 1862, the first trains operated over this line" - the L&HR's own 1960 centennial history; american-rails.com concurs). It was worked under contract by the Erie - "manned by Erie crews with Erie motive power and equipment" - as part of the 6 ft gauge Erie, so the trains are drawn as the Erie's (Erie Railway 1861-1878, New York, Lake Erie and Western from 1878). Fowler's 1875 Official Guide letter (y) at Chester, Sugar Loaf, Lake and Warwick (terminus) independently confirms an 1875 passenger year. Ends in 1880 when the arrangement was discontinued, the line was standard-gauged, and the Warwick Valley took over its own working (company history; the month is not given) - continues as feature warwick-valley-greycourt-warwick. The company history also says the WV trains "ran through to Newburgh over the Erie branch line"; that is Erie track and is not drawn here. Headway 360 min is an estimate; no timetable was read.

segments.note: The Lehigh and Hudson River Railway took over the ex-Warwick Valley line on its formation, 1 Apr 1882 (company history; en.wikipedia); the through line to Belvidere opened 14 Aug 1882. Last passenger train 8 Jul 1939: "Last run of last Lehigh & Hudson River Railway passenger service between Greycourt and Warwick, N.Y.; it is hereafter freight-only" (PRR General Chronology 1939, read directly); en.wikipedia and the company history ("in July, 1939, all passenger service was discontinued") agree. Touch-downs between: Fowler z (1893 Official Guide); the Jan 1930 Official Guide (schedule of 29 Sep 1929), read directly - 8 trains each way on weekdays, some "Motor Car" runs, connecting with the Erie at Greycourt; Fowler "Chester 1933G" (1933 Official Guide). Passenger revenue fell from $116,000 (1914) to $1,380 (1938). The L&HR was owned jointly by connecting railroads (CNJ, DL&W, Erie, LV, PRR, Reading) but kept its own officers, crews and engines throughout - stock ownership, not a change of operator. After 1939 freight only (the Feb 1952 Official Guide prints the L&HR as "FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY"). Headway 120 min reflects the 1929 timetable only and is an estimate for every other year.

segments.note: Full L&HR line Belvidere - Greycourt opened 14 Aug 1882 (en.wikipedia; american-rails.com). Fowler z (1893 Official Guide) on every station Vernon - Buttzville. Busiest 1912-1916, when the PRR/New Haven Federal Express (Boston - Washington) ran Maybrook - Belvidere over this line; automatic block signals were installed by 1913 partly for it. ICC accident report of 1925 shows scheduled first-class mixed trains with combination baggage-passenger cars. The Jan 1930 Official Guide (schedule of 29 Sep 1929, image read directly) shows weekday train 3 (Greycourt 8:10 - Easton 11:50 a.m.) and train 8 (Easton 1:10 - Greycourt 5:10 p.m.), and Sunday trains 51/58 Greycourt - Belvidere, with times at every station. [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1930 by the January 1930 Official Guide. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - service was "truncated several times over the course of the late 1920's and 1930's" (en.wikipedia) and the cut-back points and dates were not found; the real end lies somewhere 1930-1939 (by 1939 only Greycourt - Warwick remained). american-rails.com (from Classic Trains) says a 1928 Brill gas-electric worked mixed trains west of Warwick "until a crossing wreck in 1931" - uncited and unverified. Do not extend without evidence. After 1939 freight only; Belvidere - Limecrest abandoned after 1988 (not a passenger date). Headway 720 min is an estimate (the 1929 schedule shows one weekday train each way through to Easton plus a Sunday pair).

segments.note: L&HR trains over the Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Delaware track (trackage agreement 1889, 99 years - company history and american-rails.com; en.wikipedia's Bel-Del article says 1882 - CONFLICT, recorded) and over the L&HR-leased South Easton and Phillipsburg bridge into Easton. The Bel-Del is PRR track used by trackage rights; drawn in L&HR colour because the L&HR ran these trains (the PRR's own Bel-Del trains are not drawn on this map yet). Evidence: en.wikipedia's Poughkeepsie Bridge Route article lists "Lehigh and Hudson River Railway: Easton to Maybrook" as the operator of that leg of the 1890-1893 Boston - Harrisburg/Washington through trains (uncited list), and the company history says "In September, 1890, through trains began operating between Easton, Pa. and Maybrook". Collapsed to 1891 because the Easton bridge opening is in conflict (January 1890 per the company history vs 2 Oct 1890 per american-rails.com and en.wikipedia). [OPEN] START AND END: 1891 is the first and 1893 the last CONFIRMED year, not known dates - no source dates the first or last L&HR passenger train on this leg. L&HR use 1894-1928 is plausible (the 1925 ICC report describes the railway as "between Easton, Pa., and Maybrook") but no passenger timetable was seen; the gap is deliberate. Do not extend or join without evidence. Headway 720 min is an estimate (a day express and a sleeper).

segments.note: The Pennsylvania / New Haven Federal Express (Boston - Washington) ran Maybrook - Greycourt - Belvidere over the L&HR from 19 Oct 1912 to 9 Jan 1916 (en.wikipedia; the company history says October 1912 to "the completion of the Hell Gate Bridge in 1916"), rerouted off the Harlem River - Jersey City car float onto the all-rail Maybrook - Poughkeepsie Bridge - L&HR - Bel-Del route; discontinued "due to freight congestion on the Maybrook Line" and resumed via Hell Gate 1 Apr 1917. HAULING RAILROAD UNVERIFIED: the company history says the train "was operated over the Poughkeepsie bridge to the L&H at Maybrook, from there to the Pennsylvania Railroad at Belvidere", which reads as L&HR handling, so it is drawn in L&HR colour; no source names the engines or crews. If PRR or New Haven crews ran through, this segment should carry that operator instead. Only this Greycourt - Maybrook piece needs the segment - Greycourt - Belvidere is already drawn for these years by the L&HR locals. Whether L&HR locals also ran to Maybrook in these years is not established. Headway 1440 min: one train each way.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] single proven year. ICC Bureau of Safety report on the accident near Greycourt of 17 Jul 1925: "Eastbound mixed train No. 6 consisted of one milk car, one box car, one gondola car, and a combination baggage and passenger car", leaving Greycourt, where "it assumed the schedule of train No. 6, a first-class train", for Maybrook, with conductor and baggagemaster aboard - a mixed train carrying passengers, which counts as passenger service. Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed: in the Jan 1930 Official Guide (schedule of 29 Sep 1929) the Maybrook - Burnside - Hamptonburgh - Greycourt section is printed with every train column empty (no advertised passenger train), though an unadvertised mixed could still have run. Do not widen this anchor or join it to the 1912-1916 segment. Headway 1440 min is an estimate (one mixed each way).
